sections.title: Objective type questions: each has two parts of 1 mark.

questions.q: Match: (a) Prop roots (b) Haustorium (c) Sweet potato (d) Floating roots with (i) Storage (ii) Jussiaea (iii) Banyan (iv) Cuscuta.
Name the modification: (a) Rhizophora roots coming up from the marsh (b) Roots of Cuscuta.
questions.answer: (a) Pneumatophores (respiratory roots). (b) Sucking roots (haustoria).

questions.q: Fill in the blanks: (a) The lateral roots arise from the ______. (b) The number of xylem patches in a dicot root is ______ to six.
questions.answer: (a) pericycle. (b) two.

questions.q: State true or false: (a) The cambium is absent in a monocot root. (b) Roots are positively phototropic.
questions.answer: (a) True. (b) False – roots are negatively phototropic.

questions.q: Name the type of root modification and one example for storage: (a) swollen in the middle (b) spherical at the base.
questions.answer: (a) Fusiform; radish. (b) Napiform; turnip.

questions.q: Name the layers formed by the cork cambium on its outer and inner sides.
questions.answer: Outside: cork (phellem). Inside: secondary cortex (phelloderm).

questions.q: Name the two regions of the maturation zone of the root.
questions.answer: Root hair (piliferous) region and the permanent region.

questions.q: In a tetrarch root, how many lateral roots form in one row?
questions.answer: Four, equal to the number of xylem bundles.

sections.title: Very short answer questions. Answer in 30–50 words.

questions.q: Identify the modified root in the following: (1) Rhizophora (2) Cuscuta (3) Banyan (4) Sugarcane (5) Money plant.
questions.answer: (1) Pneumatophores. (2) Haustoria (sucking roots). (3) Prop roots. (4) Stilt roots. (5) Climbing roots.

questions.q: Differentiate between tap root and fibrous root systems (two points).
questions.answer: A tap root system has a persistent primary root with branches, going deep and giving strong anchorage; a fibrous system has a cluster of thin roots from the stem base, which is shallow.

questions.q: What is the quiescent centre?
questions.answer: A group of inactive cells between the root cap and the active meristem; they become active when the meristem is damaged.

questions.q: What are passage cells?
questions.answer: Endodermal cells opposite the protoxylem without Casparian strips, through which water and salts pass from the cortex into the xylem.

questions.q: State two functions of roots.
questions.answer: Anchoring the plant in the soil and absorbing water and mineral salts.

questions.q: Why are carrot, radish and turnip considered roots?
questions.answer: They are fleshy, have no nodes or buds and bear lateral roots; they store food and develop from the radicle.

questions.q: What is meant by exarch xylem?
questions.answer: The protoxylem lies towards the periphery and the metaxylem towards the centre.

questions.q: What is periderm?
questions.answer: The protective layers of phellogen, phellem and phelloderm formed in secondary growth.

sections.title: Short answer questions. Answer in 50–80 words.

questions.q: Give any three differences between a dicot root and a monocot root.
questions.answer: Dicot root: 2-6 xylem bundles, small pith, secondary growth present. Monocot root: many bundles (polyarch), large pith, no secondary growth.

questions.q: Describe the regions of the root tip.
questions.answer: Root cap protects the apex; meristematic zone divides; elongation zone makes the root longer; maturation zone has root hairs for absorption and a permanent zone producing lateral roots.

questions.q: Write about the modifications of tap root for food storage.
questions.answer: Conical (carrot), fusiform (radish), napiform (turnip) and tuberous (four o'clock plant): they are swollen and fleshy for storing food.

questions.q: Explain how lateral roots originate.
questions.answer: They arise endogenously from the pericycle opposite the protoxylem; the cells divide to form a hump which pushes through the endodermis and cortex and emerges as a branch; the number of lateral roots equals the number of xylem bundles.

questions.q: Describe the adventitious roots modified for support.
questions.answer: Prop roots (banyan) hang from branches and support them; stilt roots (sugarcane) grow obliquely from the lower nodes; climbing roots (money plant) clasp the support.

questions.q: What are pneumatophores? Where are they found and what is their function?
questions.answer: Respiratory roots that grow vertically upward out of marshy water with minute pores; found in mangroves such as Rhizophora; they help in gaseous exchange.

sections.title: Long answer questions. Answer in 80–120 words.

questions.q: Identify the modified adventitious root in the following: (1) Rhizophora (2) Cuscuta (3) Banyan (4) Sugarcane (5) Money plant. Mention the function of each.
questions.answer: (1) Pneumatophores: gas exchange. (2) Haustoria: absorb food from the host. (3) Prop roots: support. (4) Stilt roots: support. (5) Climbing roots: attach to the support.

questions.q: Describe the secondary growth in a dicot root.
questions.answer: A cambium ring forms from the conjunctive tissue and pericycle; it adds secondary phloem outside and secondary xylem inside; cork cambium arises from the pericycle and forms cork and secondary cortex; the periderm protects the root and the epiblema, cortex and endodermis peel off.

questions.q: Describe the internal structure of a dicot root.
questions.answer: Epiblema with root hairs, cortex, endodermis with Casparian strips and passage cells, pericycle, radial vascular bundles with exarch xylem, conjunctive tissue and a small pith.

questions.q: Explain the adventitious root modifications for storage, photosynthesis and absorption of moisture.
questions.answer: Tuberous (sweet potato), fasciculated (dahlia), nodulose (mango ginger), moniliform and annulated store food; assimilatory roots photosynthesise; epiphytic roots absorb moisture using velamen.
